  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION AND ACCESSIBILITY
  PLEASE SILENCE CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION

Viewing of City Council Meetings:
  • In-person – City Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206
  • Live Broadcast via Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-verse,
  channel 99. Meetings are also streamed on the City webpage, glendaleca.gov/live, on
  YouTube.com/myglendale, and on the Cablecast app under "Glendale TV". Meetings are also
  archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
City Council meeting agenda packets, any agenda related documents, and additional documents
are available at City Hall and online for public viewing on the City’s website:
https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

ADA Accessibility and Translation Services:
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services; please direct all accessibility requests to (818) 548-2090. For
translations, please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of
City provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or
speak in their native language.

Public participation in Council meetings may occur as follows:
  • In-person – City Council Chambers
  • Telephonic participation: Call (818) 937-8100
If you have any questions about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance including
agenda email notification, please contact the City Clerk’s Office via email at
CityClerk@GlendaleCA.gov, or by phone at (818) 548-2090.

   PUBLIC COMMENT GUIDELINES
The City Council welcomes public input at City Council meetings. Public input at Council meetings
is regulated by the City Council’s Rules of Order, Procedure and Decorum for the Conduct of City
Council Meetings as set forth in Resolution No. 25-76, which will be summarized below.

Written Comments and Documents:
Public comments received in writing will NOT be read aloud at the meeting but will be part of the
meeting record. Written public comments can be emailed to citycouncil@glendaleca.gov, and will
be uploaded to the City website as an attachment to the agenda item. When submitting a public
comment, please make sure to include the following:
  1. Name (optional); and
  2. Agenda item to which you are submitting public comment
  3. Submit no later than 12:00 p.m. on the day of the City Council meeting. Correspondence
  received after this time may not be distributed until the following business day.
All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours
prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City
Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, Room 110, Glendale, CA 91206.

Public Comments During Council Meeting:
Public Comments during Community Event Announcements, First and Second Periods of Oral
Communications and agenda items will be governed as provided in the descriptions for those items
on the agenda below. Pursuant to State law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on any
item not appearing on the meeting agenda, except that members of the City Council or staff may
ask a question for clarification or briefly respond to statements made or questions posed by
persons exercising public testimony rights (Government Code Section 54954.2). Staff may be
asked to follow up on such items.

Submitting Speaker Cards or Calling In for Public Comment:
Speaker cards must be submitted and telephonic participants must call in and be in the call-in
queue as follows:
  • Community Event Announcements or First or Second Period of Oral Communications: PRIOR
  TO the commencement of the specific comment period
  • Consent Calendar Items: BEFORE a motion is made on the consent calendar
  • Other agenda items, including Action items: PRIOR to the completion of the verbal staff report
  (unless waived by the Mayor)
Any audio-visual files displayed by speakers must be emailed to the Clerk’s office by 12:00 pm on
the day before a Council meeting.

  5.  CITY COUNCIUSTAFF COMMENTS (Including reports from conferences and
  regional meetings)

  Councilmember Gharpetian stated that he supports including public speaker comments
  as part of the minutes. He also suggested that when there are lengthy "Presentation and
  Appointments" items planned for a Council meeting agenda, that portion of the meeting
  be moved to the afternoon. Regarding building code changes, he asked staff to look into
  how mixed-use projects are defined with respect to the ratio of various uses and parking
  requirements for smaller mixed-use projects seeking to expand.

  Councilmember Gharpetian also commented on the recent withdrawal of a Historic
  District application for Verdugo Woodlands, seeking clarification on the survey
  component in relation to the application and the process for reactivating the application if
  the applicants wish to do so. Regarding the use of rat poison outdoors, he asked
  whether the City has a relevant law and requested a staff report or memo on the topic.
  Lastly, he asked the City Manager or City Attorney for an update regarding his idea to
  file a test case against the State for various unfunded mandates, such as housing laws
  like SB 79.

  Councilmember Kassakhian joined the meeting at 6:32 PM.

n  Councilmember Brotman agreed with Councilmember Gharpetian's comments on the
  building and safety code and stated that he believed the issue of subterranean parking
  had been addressed previously by the Council. He also noted that the City does not use
  rat poison but said he was unsure of the rules governing its use by the public. He asked
  staff to investigate whether the City previously provided bear-resistant trash cans, and if
  so, why that practice was discontinued. He expressed concern for those in Jamaica,
  Cuba, and other islands in the path of Hurricane Melissa, which appears to be one of the
  worst hurricanes on record. Lastly, he stated, "Go Dodgers."

  Councilmember Kassakhian apologized for his tardiness due to traffic congestion coming
  from a meeting across Los Angeles. He expressed that his thoughts and prayers are
  with the family of San Bernardino Sheriff's Deputy Andrew Nunez, who was killed in the
  line of duty while responding to a domestic violence call, noting that this is a reminder
  that those who serve in public safety often put their lives at risk for the sake of others.
  Regarding the need for Councilmembers to recuse themselves from certain agenda
  items, he asked staff to agendize a discussion on what information should be provided
  so the public is aware of the specific reason for a recusal. He also suggested creating a
  required document explaining the recusal to be filed with the minutes of the meeting, so
  it remains on record.

  Mayor Najarian seconded Councilmember Kassakhian's request to agendize this matter
  with priority. Councilmember Kassakhian gave an example, noting that City Attorney
  Michael Garcia had informed him of a particular conflict he has with the proposed Bus
  Rapid Transit route along Glenoaks because of the proximity of his home.

D  Mayor Najarian shared several upcoming events happening in the City:
  • October 30, 2025: YWCA Purple Tie Awards and Press Event in partnership with
  the Commission on the Status of Women - "Glendale Fire Stations as Domestic
  Violence Safe Havens," at Fire Station 21 from 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM.
  • November 1, 2025: Dia de Los Muertos at Central Library from 4:00 PM to 7:00
  PM.
  • November 1, 2025: Glendale Health Festival at Pacific Park from 9:00 AM to 2:00
  PM.
